title: Who Are the People of Palestine?
subtitle: A beginner's guide to Palestinian identity, community, faith, and ties to home
summary: Palestinians are a diverse people shaped by family, Arabic language and culture, religious life, shared memory, and ties to historic Palestine. They include Muslims, Christians, and people of other or no faith; people living in the land and across a worldwide diaspora; refugees and non-refugees; and many political views. Learning who they are begins with people, not slogans.

sections.title: Who Are the People of Palestine?
sections.body: Palestinians are not one party, armed group, or political opinion. They are families and communities with varied beliefs and experiences. Most share Arabic language and culture and a lasting connection to historic Palestine, whether they live there or in the diaspora.

sections.title: A People With More Than One Story
sections.body:
Palestinian identity is national, cultural, local, and personal. A person may also identify with a city or village, an extended family, an Arab heritage, a church or Muslim community, or a country of residence. These loyalties can exist together.

Historian [Rashid Khalidi](https://cup.columbia.edu/book/palestinian-identity/9780231150743) traces how Palestinian national consciousness grew alongside local, Arab, Ottoman, and religious loyalties. [Beshara Doumani's social history](https://www.ucpress.edu/book/9780520203709/rediscovering-palestine) shows the towns, farms, family networks, trade, and institutions of Ottoman Palestine. Their work explains why Palestinian identity has deep roots while also taking a modern national form.

Recognizing Palestinian identity does not erase Jewish, Christian, Muslim, Samaritan, Armenian, Bedouin, or other connections to the land. Honest history can acknowledge more than one community's attachment without denying another's humanity.

sections.title: Home, Diaspora, and Refugee Experience
sections.body:
Palestinians live in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, in Gaza, in Israel, in neighboring Arab countries, and around the world. Displacement in 1948 and 1967 made exile and family separation central to many Palestinian stories, but refugee is not a synonym for Palestinian. Many Palestinians are not registered refugees, and Palestinian life is much broader than displacement.

[UNRWA uses a specific operational definition](https://www.unrwa.org/palestine-refugees) for the Palestine refugees eligible for its services. That definition should not be mistaken for a complete definition of the Palestinian people. Families also preserve identity through memory, food, music, worship, education, professions, and relationships with towns and villages.

A dedicated timeline can explain wars, political organizations, and negotiations. This article keeps the focus on the people themselves.

sections.title: Start With Human Dignity
sections.body:
Begin with names, families, work, worship, art, grief, and hope. Distinguish civilians from governments, parties, and armed groups. Do not treat Muslim and Christian Palestinians as if they have identical experiences, and do not make any individual answer for an entire people.

The Quran commands believers to stand firmly for justice even against their own interests (Quran 4:135). It also says that peoples and tribes were made so that human beings may know one another, not claim racial or national superiority (Quran 49:13). For a Muslim, learning about Palestinians truthfully is therefore part of justice and human dignity.

sections.title: Key Takeaways: Who Are the People of Palestine?
sections.body: Palestinians are a diverse people, not a political stereotype. Their identity joins family, culture, faith, memory, and ties to home. Some live in historic Palestine; others live in a wide diaspora; some are refugees and others are not. Islam asks readers to meet this human story with truth, justice, and compassion.

quranVerses.arabic: ۞ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَوِ ٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ وَٱلْأَقْرَبِينَ ۚ إِن يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًۭا فَٱللَّهُ أَوْلَىٰ بِهِمَا ۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ ٱلْهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ وَإِن تَلْوُۥٓا۟ أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًۭا
quranVerses.translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So follow not [personal] inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍۢ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَٰكُمْ شُعُوبًۭا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتْقَىٰكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌۭ
quranVerses.translation: O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.

furtherReading.title: Palestinian Identity: The Construction of Modern National Consciousness
furtherReading.author: Rashid Khalidi
furtherReading.note: A major scholarly study of the development of Palestinian national consciousness; read alongside other historians for differing emphases.

furtherReading.title: Rediscovering Palestine: Merchants and Peasants in Jabal Nablus, 1700-1900
furtherReading.author: Beshara B. Doumani
furtherReading.note: A social and economic history of Ottoman Palestine that grounds national-identity discussions in local institutions, families, and regional life.

furtherReading.title: The Israel-Palestine Conflict: A History
furtherReading.author: James L. Gelvin
furtherReading.note: An accessible survey that places Palestinian identity, the Mandate, 1948, 1967, the PLO, and the Intifadas within the wider conflict.

furtherReading.title: Palestine Refugees
furtherReading.author: United Nations Relief and Works Agency
furtherReading.note: UNRWA's official explanation of its operational refugee definition and where registered Palestine refugees live. It describes an agency category, not every Palestinian.
